cf.title: QoL improvements for pgindent and combining pgindent, pgperltidy, pgperlcritic and pgperlsyncheck into one tool

input.subject: Add "format" target to make and ninja to run pgindent and pgperltidy

verdict_reasoning: The pgindent fixes in 0001 to 0004 have support in the thread, but three design choices in v4 lack agreement. Two committers object to the project shipping get_perltidy (already-exists-1, maintenance-fit-1). The README makes all tools the default, which no reviewer asked for (demand-2). Moving pgindent into pgcheck leaves the objection in message #12 unanswered (maintenance-fit-2). Nobody has replied to v4.

brief.title: Unify pgindent and Perl tools into one pgcheck script, with usability fixes
brief.problem: Running the source formatters is hard, mostly for new contributors. pgindent needs pg_bsd_indent in PATH and, with meson, picks up files in the build directory when run on "./". pgperltidy needs exactly perltidy 20230309, and pgperltidy, pgperlcritic and pgperlsyncheck lack pgindent flags such as --commit, --check, --diff and --jobs.
brief.proposed_design: v1 added a make/ninja "format" target. v4 drops that and changes the scripts: pgindent finds files with git ls-files, defaults to the current directory, runs in parallel and searches build directories for pg_bsd_indent. A new src/tools/pgcheck/pgcheck combines pgindent, pgperltidy, pgperlcritic and pgperlsyncheck, keeps the old scripts as wrappers, and adds a get_perltidy script that downloads, verifies and installs perltidy into the source tree.
user_visible_surface: New developer tool src/tools/pgcheck/pgcheck with options such as --pgindent, --perltidy, --perlcritic, --perl-syncheck, --commit, --check, --diff and --jobs.
New script src/tools/pgindent/get_perltidy that installs perltidy 20230309 into src/tools/pgindent/perltidy/.
pgindent with no arguments indents the current directory and, on a directory search, skips files git does not track.
pgperltidy, pgperlcritic and pgperlsyncheck become wrappers around pgcheck and accept its flags.
v1 only: "make format" and "ninja -C build format" targets, which v4 drops.
author_claims: Parallel runs cut a full pgindent run from about 7 seconds to 1 second, and with perltidy from over a minute to about 7 seconds.
get_perltidy checks signatures, so it is safer than the current README, which tells users to download an unverified tarball.
Easier perltidy runs could later let perltidy run on every commit, like pgindent, though merging does not force that.
Postgres developers all use git, so git ls-files is an acceptable dependency.
The author says Claude Code wrote most of the v2 code; he reviewed it but is not a Perl expert.
brief.thread_state: Peter Eisentraut committed the two temp-file cleanup patches and then removed himself as reviewer. Tom Lane wants the perltidy integration and get_perltidy rejected as a supply-chain risk, Daniel Gustafsson has the same worry, and Andrew Dunstan supported unifying the tools; nobody has replied to v4, which needs a rebase.
unclear: v4 does not show whether pgcheck runs perltidy by default or only when the right version is present, as Andrew Dunstan suggested.
The material does not say which key or signature get_perltidy checks, or where that trust anchor comes from.
The material does not say whether parallel runs work on Windows, where Andrew Dunstan noted fork() can be unreliable.
The material does not say how pgcheck behaves outside a git tree, such as non-core trees that use pgindent.
The material does not say whether the new default directory behaviour also applies to the Perl tools through pgcheck.

objections.title: get_perltidy commits the project to owning a downloader for CPAN code
objections.failure_scenario: CPAN moves the tarball, or the signing key that get_perltidy trusts is rotated or compromised. A developer then runs src/tools/pgindent/get_perltidy, and it either fails or installs code that the project's own script told them to trust. Some committer must fix the script on every supported branch.
objections.argument: pg_bsd_indent became a commit requirement only after it lived in the tree, and Tom Lane says in message #19 that perltidy will never be in the tree and that no cleanup makes 0007 acceptable. Daniel Gustafsson raises the same supply-chain concern in message #17. The author says in message #20 that signature checks make the script safer than the README's unverified tarball, but the proposal does not say which key is checked or who maintains that trust anchor. The script also removes the manual install instructions, which Daniel asked to keep.
objections.author_must_show: Which key does get_perltidy verify, where does that trust anchor come from, and which committer updates it when it changes?

critic.reasoning: Two committers object to the project shipping an installer, and 0007 removes the manual instructions that message #17 asked to keep. The script is one separable patch, so dropping it leaves 0001 to 0006 intact, which makes this fixable.

objections.title: pgcheck ties pgindent to Perl tools with a different lifecycle
objections.failure_scenario: The project moves to a newer perltidy, or changes pgperlcritic rules. That change now edits the same script that every committer runs before each C commit and at the release-time indent run. A later pgindent fix on master also no longer applies cleanly to back branches, which still have src/tools/pgindent/pgindent.
objections.argument: Peter Eisentraut objected in message #12 that these tools run at different times and update differently, and he preferred separate make subtargets. v4 answers this by moving pgindent into a new combined pgcheck script (0005, 0006). That makes the coupling larger, and no committer has replied to v4. The useful pgindent changes in 0001 to 0004 do not need the merge.
objections.author_must_show: Why must pgindent itself move into pgcheck, when 0001 to 0004 could land alone and the Perl tools could share code without the move?

critic.reasoning: Peter Eisentraut's objection in message #12 has no answer in v4, which widens the coupling, and 0001 to 0004 do not need the merge. The back-branch part is weak, because the wrappers keep the old command names and pgindent fixes are rarely back-patched.

objections.title: Git-only directory search changes behaviour for non-core trees
objections.failure_scenario: An extension maintainer runs pgindent on a directory in a tree that is not a git checkout, such as an unpacked tarball or another VCS. The directory search finds no tracked files and processes nothing, or exits with an error. The maintainer finds out only when their CI stops reformatting.
objections.argument: Peter Eisentraut noted in message #18 that pgindent is also used on trees that are not stock Postgres. The author answers in message #13 that all Postgres developers use git. v4 still indents files that are named explicitly, but the proposal does not say what a directory search does outside a git tree.
objections.author_must_show: What does pgindent or pgcheck do on a directory argument outside a git work tree, and does it keep the old directory walk there?

critic.reasoning: Message #13 answers only for core developers, and message #18 later names non-stock trees as users of pgindent. The 0001 commit message does not say what a directory search does outside a git work tree.

objections.title: get_perltidy repeats a one-line cpanm command and adds a download path
objections.failure_scenario: The project ships get_perltidy, so it now owns a downloader, its trust anchor and its URL handling. When CPAN changes a mirror, key or archive layout, the script breaks for everyone using it. The README no longer gives the manual cpanm instructions to fall back on.
objections.argument: Message #10 shows that `cpanm -l $HOME/perltidy-20230309 Perl::Tidy@20230309` installs the exact version in one command, and pgperltidy already checks the version (message #4). The author answers that get_perltidy verifies signatures (message #20), but the material does not say which key it checks or where that key comes from. Messages #17 and #19 object to the project taking responsibility for installing code. Message #17 also asks to keep the manual instructions, yet the v4 README hunk removes them.
objections.author_must_show: What does get_perltidy verify that the documented cpanm command does not, which key does it trust, and why must the project ship and maintain that check?

critic.reasoning: The cpanm command in message #10 installs the exact version in one step, so the existing route can do the job. The author's signature argument cannot be weighed against it until the proposal says what the script verifies.

objections.title: Combining perltidy into the default run rests on a policy nobody agreed to
objections.failure_scenario: A contributor runs src/tools/pgcheck/pgcheck with no arguments, as the README suggests, and with the right perltidy installed it also reformats Perl files the patch never touched. The contributor finds out when the diff picks up unrelated files and must be cleaned by hand.
objections.argument: The pgcheck README says it runs all tools on the current directory by default. Message #2 notes that perltidy is not enforced, so whole-tree runs change files outside the patch. The stated reason for combining the tools is to get perltidy run on every commit (message #13), but message #20 calls that policy a separate, later discussion, and Peter Eisentraut (message #12) says the tools run at different times in practice. Andrew Dunstan (message #4) wanted unification only with perltidy off unless a flag is given.
objections.author_must_show: Who, apart from the author, wants pgindent and the Perl tools to run together by default before perltidy is enforced on commits?

critic.reasoning: The README makes all tools the default, and message #2 reports that perltidy changes files outside the patch because the tree is not kept perltidy-clean. Message #4 supported unification only with perltidy behind a flag, and v4 does not answer that.

other_surviving.title: Bare pgcheck runs every tool, including the version-pinned perltidy
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A new contributor follows the README and runs `src/tools/pgcheck/pgcheck` with no options. Without perltidy 20230309 the run fails on the version check. With some other perltidy, Perl files outside the patch get reformatted. Either way the contributor first meets the exact hurdle the patch set aims to remove.
other_surviving.argument: The pgcheck README says that by default it runs all tools on the current directory. Message #2 asks for perltidy to be optional, and in message #4 Andrew Dunstan's support depends on perltidy staying off unless a flag is given and the right version is present. In message #12 Peter Eisentraut prefers separate format-c and format-perl targets for users who lack some tools. v4 does not say how the default copes when perltidy is missing or has the wrong version.
other_surviving.author_must_show: When perltidy 20230309 is not installed, does a bare pgcheck run skip perltidy, warn, or fail, and do the pgindent and pgperltidy wrappers keep their old exit codes?

critic.reasoning: The pgcheck README says a bare run uses all tools, and v4 does not say what happens when perltidy 20230309 is absent. The wrong-version branch of the scenario should be dropped, because pgperltidy already checks the version (message #4).

other_surviving.title: get_perltidy does not say what its signature check trusts
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A developer runs src/tools/pgindent/get_perltidy, which fetches Perl-Tidy from CPAN and installs it into the source tree. If the check trusts a key or checksum fetched from the same source, a compromised mirror or CPAN account passes it. The developer then runs that code on every pgcheck call, and nothing alerts them.
other_surviving.argument: In message #19 Tom Lane calls the script a supply-chain risk, and Daniel Gustafsson raises the same concern in message #17. In message #20 the author answers that signature checks make get_perltidy safer than the README, which installs an unverified tarball. The README hunk only says the script "downloads, verifies, and installs", so a committer cannot judge that answer without the trust anchor. A hash or key committed in our tree would be a real anchor; a signature fetched with the tarball would not be.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Which key or checksum does get_perltidy verify against, where does it come from, and is it committed in the tree instead of fetched at run time?

critic.reasoning: The author's answer in message #20 depends on the signature check, but the README hunk only says "verifies". The proposal does not name the key or checksum, or say whether it is committed in the tree.

other_surviving.title: No committer who knows these Perl tools has taken ownership of v4
other_surviving.failure_scenario: pgcheck goes in, and a parallel run then fails on Windows or drops files with unusual names. Every committer hits the bug before committing, but the author has said he is not a Perl expert. The only reviewer who engaged has stepped back.
other_surviving.argument: Message #11 says an AI wrote most of the code, and in message #13 the author says he is not a Perl expert. Peter Eisentraut committed two small patches and then removed himself as reviewer. Andrew Dunstan supported unifying the tools in message #4, but he has not reviewed v4. Every committer depends on this script before each commit.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Which committer familiar with pgindent and the Perl tools will review pgcheck and own fixes to it after commit?

critic.reasoning: The facts hold: nobody replied to v4, the reviewer withdrew, and the Windows fork() question from message #14 is open. This is a committability concern and should not count against the design.

refuted.title: get_perltidy does not meet the condition the project set for pgindent
refuted.failure_scenario: A new contributor runs src/tools/pgindent/get_perltidy as the README now tells them to, and it fetches and installs third-party Perl code from CPAN into the source tree. If that upstream release or its signing key is compromised, the project's own script installs it on developer and committer machines. Developers under corporate rules against unapproved Perl modules have no documented route left, because 0007 removes the manual install instructions.
refuted.argument: Messages #8 and #19 report that pgindent cleanliness was required only after pg_bsd_indent was brought into the tree, which gave one managed version per branch and a safe way to get it. Perltidy will not be vendored (#8, #9), so get_perltidy has to supply that safety from outside the tree. The author answers in #20 that signature checks make the script safer than the current README, but the material does not say which key is checked or where that trust anchor comes from. Daniel Gustafsson (#17) shares the concern and asked that the installation instructions be kept, which the README hunk in 0007 does not do.
refuted.author_must_show: Which key does get_perltidy verify against, who maintains that trust anchor per branch, and why should the manual install instructions be dropped?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1 and security-1. Its framing around the pgindent-cleanliness condition is also answered in message #20, which says merging does not make perltidy a commit requirement.

refuted.title: Git-only directory search changes pgindent behaviour for non-git and untracked trees
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension developer runs `pgindent .` on a source tree unpacked from a release tarball, or on new files not yet added to git. With v4-0001 the directory search finds no tracked files, so nothing is indented. The developer may only notice when a reviewer reports style problems.
refuted.argument: In message #18 Peter Eisentraut notes that pgindent also runs against trees that are not stock Postgres. The author answered in message #13 that all Postgres developers use git, but that covers core work only, not the out-of-tree users Peter named. The proposal does not say what happens outside a git work tree: an error, a silent empty run, or a fallback to the old file search. Today `pgindent dir` indents what is in the directory, and v4 changes that without an option to keep the old behaviour.
refuted.author_must_show: What does a directory run of pgindent or pgcheck do outside a git work tree, and how can a user get the old file search back?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-4. Its untracked-file case is the documented intent of 0001, which still indents files named explicitly on the command line.

refuted.title: get_perltidy serves few users, and a one-line workaround exists
refuted.failure_scenario: The project ships get_perltidy for the small group that runs perltidy today. A CPAN mirror, a signing key or the script's checks later need changing, and a committer must answer for a script that installed code on developer machines. The only gain over the existing cpanm one-liner is one shorter command.
refuted.argument: Message #15 says perltidy is run only by a subset of committers, and message #10 gives `cpanm -l ... Perl::Tidy@20230309` as a single command that already works. The thread has no request from anyone else for a download script. Tom Lane (messages #8 and #19) and Daniel Gustafsson (message #17) see the security cost as falling on the project as a whole. The author answers in message #20 that the signature check is safer than the README, but that improves the README, and does not show that more people need the script.
refuted.author_must_show: Which contributors outside the current perltidy users have asked for this, and why does the cpanm one-liner from message #10 not serve them?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1. Its count of users is also weak evidence, because message #15 gives the install burden as the reason few people run perltidy today.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: get_perltidy downloads third-party Perl code and installs it into the source tree on developer machines.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: 0005 moves pgindent to src/tools/pgcheck/pgcheck, so master and the back branches no longer share the script.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The project takes on a combined pgcheck script, three wrappers and a downloader with a trust anchor.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: get_perltidy does a job that the cpanm command in message #10 does in one line.

questions: Which key or checksum does get_perltidy verify against, and is it committed in the tree or fetched at run time?
What does get_perltidy verify that the cpanm command in message #10 does not, and why does 0007 remove the manual install instructions?
When perltidy 20230309 is not installed, does a bare pgcheck run skip perltidy, warn, or fail?
Why must pgindent move into pgcheck, when 0001 to 0004 could be committed alone and the Perl tools could share code without the move?
What does a directory run of pgindent or pgcheck do outside a git work tree, such as an unpacked tarball?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows pgindent and the Perl tools under src/tools. Peter Eisentraut committed two small patches and then removed himself as reviewer, and no committer has replied to v4.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a script that every committer runs before each commit, including parallel runs on Windows. With 0007 the owner also signs for a downloader and its trust anchor on each branch that has it.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted four versions and moved the entry forward through October 2026. He says he is not a Perl expert, and the patch has needed a rebase since 2026-10-05.

priority.reason: Only Postgres developers and extension authors use these tools, and the patch set is about 40 KiB of Perl scripts with no backend code. 0001 to 0004 have support and can go ahead once the get_perltidy, default-run and pgcheck merge questions are settled or split off.

provisional_note: No code was read, so the signature check in get_perltidy, the parallel run on Windows and the behaviour outside a git tree could not be checked. Only 3 of 21 messages were visible; later messages are known through the objections.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add llvm version into the version string
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the LLVM version to PG_VERSION_STR, the way the gcc version is already shown, so that JIT bug reports include it. A later version takes the runtime version from the loaded library through LLVMGetVersion, an API that exists from LLVM 16 on.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the configure-time llvm-config version may not match the library loaded at run time. He also objected that changing what version() returns can break code that parses it, and that adding subsystem versions to it does not scale to ICU or libxml2. He suggested a new system view instead, the author agreed to try that direction, and others proposed showing both build-time and runtime versions in the view.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Adding rows to a view over time seems way less likely to cause
problems than messing with a string people probably have crufty
parsing code for.

precedents_retrieved.title: Unified file access using virtual file descriptors
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make virtual file descriptors (VFDs) the common interface for most non-buffer-cache, non-WAL files, adding sequential read/write, seek/tell, append and ferror-style error calls to fd.c. A second patch converts many callers from system or C library file calls to VFDs, as groundwork for transparent encryption, compression or checksums.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch failed to compile on CFbot (an undeclared MAXIMUM_VFD in fd.c), and the author did not post a new version after this was reported. The commitfest manager returned it with feedback for that reason, and no design review appears in the thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
With no update to the thread and the compilation still failing I'm
marking this as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert logical snapshot filename format change in SnapBuildSnapshotExists().
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert logical snapshot filename format change in SnapBuildSnapshotExists().
Reverted commit(s): Standardize LSN formatting by zero padding
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 2633dae2e48 standardized LSN formatting but mistakenly changed
the logical snapshot filename format in SnapBuildSnapshotExists() from
"%X-%X.snap" to "%08X-%08X.snap". Other code still used the original
"%X-%X.snap" format, causing the replication slot synchronization worker
to fail to find existing snapshot files and produce excessive log messages.

This commit restores the original "%X-%X.snap" format
in SnapBuildSnapshotExists() to resolve the issue.

precedents_retrieved.title: Package version in PG_VERSION and version()
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Michael Paquier, Peter Eisentraut, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a configure variable VENDOR_VERSION so packagers can embed a package version, such as "Debian 10.1-2", in the version() string built from PG_VERSION_STR. The main version number shown by psql and server_version would stay unchanged.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers held that the existing --with-extra-version option already does this, and that no evidence showed a new mechanism was needed. The author's concern that a changed version string breaks third-party tools was judged speculative, and Tom Lane noted that brittle version parsing could break either variant. The author then switched the Debian packages to --with-extra-version and closed the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IMO there's not really any evidence that we need an additional mechanism
in this space.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid hiding shared filesets in pg_ls_tmpdir (pg_ls_* functions for showing metadata ...)
precedents_retrieved.summary: pg_ls_tmpdir skips anything that is not a regular file, so it hides shared filesets, which are directories under pgsql_tmp. The proposal changes pg_ls_tmpdir to return an isdir column, as pg_stat_file does, so these directories show up.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Both messages are from the author, and no reviewer reply appears in the visible messages.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow an extention to be updated without a script
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an `updates_without_script` option to the extension control file that lists version pairs such as '1.1--1.2' that need no update script. ALTER EXTENSION would then accept those paths without an empty extension--old--new.sql file, and a real script, when present, would still take priority.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane argued that extension versions describe the state of the SQL objects, so a change with no update script does not need a new version, and he called the option unnecessary and confusing. Julien Rouhaud agreed that core should not add hacks for this case, even though he ships empty update scripts himself. The author withdrew the proposal because empty update scripts already solve the problem.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The point
of extension versions is to distinguish different states of the
extension's SQL objects.  We do not consider mods in underlying C code
to justify a new version.

precedents_retrieved.title: Unicode mapping scripts cleanup
precedents_retrieved.summary: A series of patches cleans up the Unicode mapping scripts in src/backend/utils/mb/Unicode/ by fixing wrong comments, missing makefile pieces and similar problems. The goal is to get the scripts working again, so that changes to the CJK mappings could be considered later.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund marked the entry returned with feedback because the thread had made little progress, even though he called the patches generally a good idea. Most of the discussion was about whether to change existing mappings, which Tatsuo Ishii said would break user applications. The author had said he was not proposing to change the mappings.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I've marked this as returned-with-feedback for now, since there hasn't
been much progress lately.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add code indentation check to cirrus-ci
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a Cirrus CI task, or a step in the SanityCheck or CompilerWarnings task, that runs pgindent and fails when a change is not pgindent-clean. The goal is to catch indentation problems in developer and cfbot CI runs before commit, so that committers spend less time on follow-up indentation fixes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the CI check puts the burden of pgindent-cleanliness on initial patch submitters, while it should be enforced at commit into the master repo. He feared it would drive novice contributors away. Andrew Dunstan saw no consensus for the change, and the author withdrew the CF entry because the idea was being discussed in a separate thread about meson targets for pgindent.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We want to enforce this at commit into the master repo, but
I fear enforcing it earlier will drive novice contributors away for
no very good reason.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make ON_ERROR_STOP stop on shell script failure
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes psql's ON_ERROR_STOP also stop a script when a shell command run from psql, such as \! false, exits with a failure status. Later versions extend ON_ERROR_STOP with values that choose whether SQL errors, shell failures or both stop the script, and cover other ways to run shell commands (backticks, \g |, \o |, \w |, \copy program).
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying and waited on its author from December 2022, and the author's email address started bouncing. The CF manager closed it as stalled. Reviewers had also questioned the design: Greg Stark found no tests and did not see why the ON_ERROR_STOP_ON, ON_ERROR_STOP_ALL and ON_ERROR_STOP_SHELL values were needed. Corey Huinker noted that the new SHELL_ERROR variable overlaps with the patch.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b0a55f4, to remove for now the TAP test that did the
equivalent of check_guc.  The test has been using pg_config --sharedir
to find the location of postgresql.conf.sample.  While the buildfarm and
normal build environments rather liked that, this proves to be an issue
for Debian where pg_config is patched to not be relocatable, causing the
test to fail.

Rather than relying on pg_config, we'd better find the sample file based
on its location from the source directory.  However, this is also an
issue as a TAP test only offers the build directory as of TESTDIR in the
environment context, so this would fail with VPATH builds.  Perhaps the
source path could be provided additionally when running the TAP tests.
Or perhaps we may be able to get away by just switching to a SQL
approach, by using PG_ABS_SRCDIR but this is going to require some extra
loops to get the sample file from the correct path in src/backend/.  In
any case, this needs more thoughts, so just revert the test case until
something better is done about this relocation problem.

roaster_notes.note: The only listed precedent [P14] is about making a pgindent check fail in CI for submitters; its reason does not apply here, because this proposal does not enforce formatting on anyone. No precedent found for unifying the tools.
The get_perltidy supply-chain concern and perltidy enforcement policy belong to other angles. Here the main gaps are the default behaviour of pgcheck and of the git-based file search.

The proposal changes only developer scripts under src/tools and README files. It touches no on-disk format, WAL, replication, catalog, wire protocol or extension ABI, so this angle has nothing to object to.

The other changes have no privilege aspect: git ls-files discovery, the default directory, parallel runs, finding pg_bsd_indent and the pgcheck wrappers. The concern about odd file names was addressed in message #21.
Objections are listed above. The precedent [P14] is about enforcing pgindent in CI, not about tooling or perltidy installs, so it is not cited.

The pgindent fixes (git ls-files, default directory, finding pg_bsd_indent, parallel runs) and the shared flags in pgcheck have no existing equivalent of the same effort, so this angle raises nothing against them.

The pgindent changes (git ls-files, current-directory default, parallel runs, finding pg_bsd_indent) have support from Tom Lane, Andrew Dunstan and Peter Eisentraut, so this angle raises nothing against them.
